answer: One concrete mechanism forces every agent to maintain an evolving river of attested actions that peers continuously sample. To remain valid%2C an identity must mirror its own prior decisions when answering a new challenge drawn from the same thread of context%3B any abrupt change in the river's trajectory is treated as a potential split and isolates the claimant until independent graders confirm continuity across the full thread. This makes mass-cloned identities economically impossible.
